title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference: September 18 | Week 1 vs. Los Angeles Chargers
headline: Jeremiyah Love's workload is undefined: LaFleur gave no carry expectation and said the 'hot hand' back will stay in the game.
summary: LaFleur said the walkthrough routine is standard and mostly about getting players' minds right before game day, not a major change. He said a defensive player on the opponent's roster is a 'chess piece' who will be treated as a linebacker even though the opponent often uses him as a nickel, and that he expects that player to play despite a groin issue. He called the opponent a well-coached team with excellent players in all three phases and downplayed motivational angles, saying the focus is simply on the opponent. On special teams, he said his unit played well in the last game but needs cleanup, and that his special teams emphasis comes through daily communication with his special teams coordinator and roster decisions. On rookie running back Jeremiyah Love, LaFleur said Love's role will not be expanded on purpose, that he has no idea how many carries Love will get, and that the team will ride whoever is hot at running back. He said Love is slowing the game down and will keep getting more comfortable as he plays more. LaFleur also noted the team is planning around a future game in a hot-weather environment and that his father visited practice.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 2 Media Availability | Friday, September 18th | Press Conference

When asked about Michael Penix Jr., Stefanski said he was not ready, that the process is progressive, and that Penix will return when he is ready; he did not rule out a return next week but said he was focused on this game. Stefanski said Strand's reps have been limited but he would be ready if needed, and that all active-roster players are trusted to play. AJ Terrell and a player named Chris are questionable, with a decision to come over the next 24 hours; a reporter suggested Chris could be a starting guard, which fits Chris Lindstrom. Za'Darius Smith is progressing from his shoulder issue and is being counted on, with his role to be expanded gradually. Stefanski praised Divine Deablo's first regular-season work with the green dot. He also praised the quarterback's off-script ability, though the name in the question was garbled in the captions, so the player is unclear. He closed by saying he was excited to coach in front of Atlanta fans at the first home game.

title: Joe Brady Breaks Down Week 2 Victory Over Detroit Lions | Buffalo Bills
headline: DJ Moore's injury is the key watch item: he is day-to-day with a possible one-game absence, while Keon Coleman, Dalton Kincaid, and Deone Walker earned praise after Week 2.
summary: Coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore's injury is not severe but he may miss one game, and the team will see how he recovers over the long weekend since there is no practice until next Wednesday. Ed Oliver was ruled out before the Lions game after a late-breaking pain report during the pregame process, and players were undergoing tests and MRIs on Friday. Brady said Josh Allen had no concerns after reports of him being unwell, calling it typical pre-Thursday-game IV treatment. On the offense, Brady said the team is still defining its identity, that the run game and Allen's aggressiveness on first downs stress defenses, and that the offense left points on the field. He praised Keon Coleman for his six catches, the key third-and-seven conversion, and his trust with Allen while filling in for Moore. Brady praised Dalton Kincaid's blocking and versatility, and said Deone Walker's two batted balls and expanded role showed he is trending up. He also said Keleki Latu's role will keep growing and that Skyler Bell is ready, though he did not name Bell as the next starter. Brady took responsibility for poor clock management on the final two-minute drive before halftime. The team now has ten days to prepare for the Chargers.
